- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤0.2) and prices are falling, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to avoid missing downward momentum.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a 2–5 day decay filter to smooth out post-spike forecasts.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.3–0.7) and price is trending, model often fails to capture mean reversion; adjust forecast toward historical 30-day average if deviation > 2σ.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to be overly optimistic in early periods (e.g., first 5–7 days); apply a 1–2% downward bias to early forecast points.
- When sentiment history shows repeated reversal patterns (e.g., bullish → bearish → bullish), model often misreads momentum; use sentiment lag (e.g., 3–5 day sentiment) to weight future price direction.
